item.title: Strongly quasidiagonal C*-algebras with nuclear dimension one and infinite decomposition rank
item.description: arXiv:2611.14888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct the first, to our knowledge, examples of strongly quasidiagonal C*-algebras with finite nuclear dimension and infinite decomposition rank. The examples are extensions of the form $0\to I \to E\to C(\mathbb{T})\to 0$ where $I$ is a simple AF-algebra. These examples are in some sense the easiest `natural' choices in light of Spielberg's work on AF-embedding extensions and the behavior of each dimension theory with respect to extensions. The standard extension bound provides $\dim_{\mathrm{nuc}} E \leq 2$ which is improved to 1 by recent work of Evington, Faurot and Schafhauser. Nuclear dimension 1 is the lowest possible for such an example because decomposition rank and nuclear dimension agree at 0. Finally, failure of the comparison property used to show infinite decomposition rank was inspired by local operator space techniques of Junge, Ozawa and Ruan.
item.dc:creator: Caleb Eckhardt

item.title: On the Equivalence of Linear and $C^*$ Extremality for Unital Completely Positive Maps on Commutative Real $C^*$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.15383v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal A$ be a unital commutative real $C^*$-algebra and $\mathcal H$ be a finite dimensional real Hilbert space. In this article, an easily verifiable necessary and sufficient condition for a linear extreme unital completely positive (UCP) map $\Phi:\mathcal A \rightarrow B(\mathcal H)$ to be C*-extreme, is obtained. As an application, the $C^*$-algebras $\mathcal A$ on which linear extreme UCP maps coincide with the $C^*$-extreme ones, are classified.
item.dc:creator: Sriram Balasubramanian, Karthikeyan Thangaraj

item.title: Cleanness and real rank zero in $C^*$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.15407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A unital $C^*$-algebra is called clean if every element is the sum of an idempotent and an invertible element. We prove that cleanness is equivalent to real rank zero. More precisely, the invertible summand can be chosen with inverse norm at most $2+\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, and the constant $2$ is optimal. In particular, every von Neumann algebra is clean, answering a question of Lam. Clean decompositions with uniformly bounded idempotent summands characterize real rank zero and stable rank one. Moreover, $*$-cleanness, defined by requiring the idempotent summands to be projections, is equivalent to real rank zero, stable rank one, and triviality of the $K_1$-group. Finally, sharp cleanness, defined by requiring clean decompositions with inverse norm at most $2$, is equivalent to real rank zero and the $SAW^*$ property.
item.dc:creator: Lu Cui, Minghui Ma, Wei Yuan

item.title: Every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra has an untwisted \'etale groupoid model
item.description: arXiv:2611.16079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that every classifiable stably finite $C^*$-algebra is isomorphic to the $C^*$-algebra of a second countable, locally compact Hausdorff, principal \'etale groupoid. Equivalently, every such $C^*$-algebra has a $C^*$-diagonal whose Weyl twist is trivial. Together with Evington and Sibbel's recent result for all UCT Kirchberg algebras, this provides untwisted principal groupoid models for every classifiable $C^*$-algebra.
item.dc:creator: Nikolay A. Ivanov, Ali I. Raad

item.title: Almost unimodular quantum groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.16136v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define a locally compact quantum group $\mathbb{G}$ to be almost unimodular if its modular element is diagonalizable. This is shown to be equivalent to the almost periodicity of a novel weight on the dual von Neumann algebra, which we call the middle Haar weight. The point modular spectrum of this weight is related to the point spectrum of $\delta$, and we prove that unimodularity of $\mathbb{G}$ is equivalent to traciality of this weight. When $\delta$ is affiliated with the center of $L^\infty(\mathbb{G})$, we show that there is a canonical closed, normal, unimodular quantum subgroup $\mathbb{G}_1 \leq \mathbb{G}$ which assumes the role of the unimodular part of $\mathbb{G}$, and moreover the openness of this quantum subgroup is equivalent to the almost periodicity of $\mathbb{G}$. Additionally, we establish several permanence properties of almost unimodularity.
item.dc:creator: Aldo Garcia Guinto, Lucas Hall, Brent Nelson

item.title: Kac lemma on noncommutative probability spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.16972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove non-commutative Kac's formula for actions of countable groups. We replace the return time functions by suitable projections in von Neumann algebras. Moreover, we prove a generalised Kac's formula in the non-commutative setting which extends the allocation construction of Meyerovitch and Weiss and is motivated by the random Kac inequality of Aaronson.
item.dc:creator: Tattwamasi Amrutam, Diptesh Saha, Xumin Wang

item.title: $C^*$-selflessness for free Burnside groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.17285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The free Burnside group $B(m,n)$ is obtained from the free group of rank $m$ by imposing the relations $w^n=1$ for all words $w$. We prove that $B(m,n)$ is completely $C^*$-selfless for every $m\geq2$ and every odd exponent $n\geq557$. Consequently, its reduced group $C^*$-algebra has stable rank one and strict comparison of positive elements by its canonical trace. This answers the question of whether $C^*$-selfless groups can satisfy a nontrivial group law. The proof establishes Ozawa's property $P_{PHP}$ by combining a combinatorial construction with a relative power-avoidance argument based on the canonical forms of Atkarskaya-Rips-Tent.
item.dc:creator: Anna Cascioli

item.title: On JT boundary algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.15452v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct the canonical boundary algebras of Jackiw--Teitelboim gravity coupled to free bosonic matter. For a nonempty finite or countable family of species with lowest weights greater than one half, the two boundary algebras are mutual commutants and nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_\infty$ factors. Their nonzero finite corners are nonhyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors. The construction uses bounded heat-regularized fields and a Hilbert algebra, which gives a faithful normal semifinite trace without a path-integral argument. The weight restriction is sharp: elementary point fields remain unbounded after positive heat regularization when $0<d\leq1/2$. For one massless scalar, specified bounded observables and normal states have a high energy limit described by a hyperfinite continuous core. We explain why this limit does not preserve the nonhyperfiniteness of the exact algebra.
item.dc:creator: Feng Xu

item.title: A Max-Flow Min-Cut Theorem for Quantum Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.15508v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose natural definitions of cuts and flows for quantum graphs. For cuts we consider two notions: ordinary cuts, which partition the vertex set into two parts; and generalised cuts, defined as a continuous relaxation of the binary partition function. We show that our definitions satisfy a max-flow min-cut theorem: For any disjoint terminal sets $S$ and $T$, the maximum value of an $S$-$T$-flow of a quantum graph equals the minimum value of a generalised $S$-$T$ cut, while the minimum value of an ordinary $S$-$T$ cut can be larger. While for classical graphs the values of the minimum generalised cut and the minimum ordinary cut coincide---recovering the classical max-flow min-cut theorem---we also show how it is more natural to think of flows as duals of generalised cuts instead of ordinary cuts.
item.dc:creator: Gian Luca Spitzer, Ion Nechita

item.title: Quasicentral modulus for almost normal operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.15604v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In 1984, Voiculescu conjectured that the Hilbert--Schmidt quasicentral modulus vanishes for every almost normal operator. We prove this conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Shiqi Liu, Hongyin Zhao

item.title: Flows on uniform Roe algebras
item.description: arXiv:2411.06999v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a uniformly locally finite metric space $(X, d)$, we investigate \emph{coarse} flows on its uniform Roe algebra $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$, defined as one-parameter groups of automorphisms whose differentiable elements include all partial isometries arising from partial translations on $X$. We first show that any flow $\sigma$ on $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$ corresponds to a (possibly unbounded) self-adjoint operator $h$ on $\ell_2(X)$ such that $\sigma_t(a) = e^{ith} a e^{-ith}$ for all $t \in \mathbb{R}$, allowing us to focus on operators $h$ that generate flows on $ \mathrm{C}^*_u (X)$. Assuming Yu's property A, we prove that a self-adjoint operator $h$ on $\ell_2(X)$ induces a coarse flow on $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$ if and only if $h$ can be expressed as $h = a + d$, where $a \in \mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$ and $d$ is a diagonal operator with entries forming a coarse function on $X$. We further study cocycle equivalence and cocycle perturbations of coarse flows, showing that, under property A, any coarse flow is a cocycle perturbation of a diagonal flow. Finally, for self-adjoint operators $h$ and $k$ that induce coarse flows on $\mathrm{C}^*_u(X)$, we characterize conditions under which the associated flows are either cocycle perturbations of each other or cocycle conjugate. In particular, if $h - k$ is bounded, then the flow induced by $h$ is a cocycle perturbation of the flow induced by $k$.
item.dc:creator: Bruno de Mendon\c{c}a Braga, Alcides Buss, Ruy Exel

item.title: Noncommutative Maximal Ergodic Theorems for Modulated $(C,\alpha)$-Averages with Operator-Valued Weights
item.description: arXiv:2609.23616v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study modulated $(C,\alpha)$-ergodic averages with operator-valued weights and their subsequential versions in the setting of semifinite von Neumann algebras. Our framework combines $(C,\alpha)$-type modulation with operator-valued weights and extends both scalar-weighted and operator-valued weighted ergodic theories. We establish mean ergodic theorems and maximal inequalities for these averages on noncommutative $L_p$-spaces. We then study bilateral almost uniform and almost uniform convergence in noncommutative Orlicz spaces, including convergence along subsequences of density one when $\alpha\geq 1$. A key ingredient in our approach is the introduction of the $p$-convexity condition on the underlying Orlicz function. This condition allows us to transfer appropriate maximal estimates from noncommutative $L_p$-spaces to establish bilateral uniform equicontinuity in measure at zero on the corresponding noncommutative $p$-convex Orlicz spaces. Together with the noncommutative Banach principle, this yields the desired pointwise convergence results. As an additional consequence of our $p$-convexity argument, we extend Rota theorem to a larger class of noncommutative Orlicz spaces associated with the $p$-convex Orlicz functions considered in this article.
item.dc:creator: Arup Chattopadhyay, Debabrata De, Disha Shaw

item.title: The Bishop--Phelps--Bollob\'as Property for Extremally Disconnected Ranges
item.description: arXiv:2606.12080v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathbb F$ be either $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $L$ be a nonempty extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space. We show that $(X,C(L,\mathbb F))$ has the Bishop--Phelps--Bollob\'as property with $\eta(\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^2/2$ for every Banach space $X$ over $\mathbb F$. For each fixed $L$ and either scalar field, this bound is optimal uniformly over $X$.
item.dc:creator: Tattwamasi Amrutam, Priyadarshi Dey, Chunlin Liu, Monika

item.title: Repeated differentiation of deterministic polynomials with asymptotically radial root distributions
item.description: arXiv:2607.16954v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent works of Galligo, Najnudel, and Vu (2025) and Najnudel and Vu (2026) study repeated differentiation for polynomials of the form $P(z)=p(z^m)$, where $p$ is a deterministic polynomial of degree $n$ with real, non-negative roots, in the regime where $m$ and $n$ are large. If $m\gg \log(n)$ and the root distribution of $P$ converges to a compactly supported, radial probability measure $\mu_0$, these works show that for $0\le t<1$, the root distribution of the $\lfloor nmt\rfloor$-th derivative of $P$ converges to a compactly supported probability measure $\mu_t$ given by an explicit formula for its radial quantile function. We give a substantially simplified proof of this result and also extend the result from repeated differentiation to repeated applications of the differential operator $z^a(d/dz)^b$. Our proof is based on new, sharp estimates on the roots of polynomial with real, non-negative roots in terms of the coefficients of the polynomial. We also compute the limiting root distribution in the case when $m$ is fixed and $n$ tends to infinity. Then letting $m$ tend to infinity we obtain the same limit as before. Along the way, we prove a generalization of the free multiplicative law of large numbers that is of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Brian C. Hall, Daniel Perales
